description: A comprehensive study of the internal structures of plants and vital biological processes, including photosynthesis, tissue conduction, and hormonal regulation.

sections.title: Plant Tissue System
sections.description: Specialized complex permanent tissues responsible for the conduction of water, minerals, and food throughout the plant body.

key_associations.extra_info: Facilitates a unidirectional flow from the roots upwards to the leaves.
Facilitates a multidirectional flow from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

important_facts.fact: Dendrochronology is the scientific method of determining the age of a tree by counting the annual rings present in its xylem.

sections.title: Photosynthesis
sections.description: The biochemical process by which autotrophic green plants synthesize their own food using sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water.

scientific_principles.application: An oxidation-reduction reaction where water is oxidized to release oxygen, and carbon dioxide is reduced to form glucose.

key_concepts.explanation: Occurs in the grana of the chloroplast and strictly requires the direct presence of sunlight.
Occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast and is light-independent (does not require direct sunlight).

important_facts.fact: The rate of photosynthesis is maximum in red light and minimum or entirely absent in green light.
Magnesium (Mg) is the central core metal ion present in the chlorophyll molecule.

sections.title: Plant Hormones (Phytohormones)
sections.description: Chemical messengers that naturally coordinate and regulate plant growth, development, and responses to environmental stimuli.

key_associations.extra_info: Promotes stem elongation, inhibits lateral bud growth, and is also used commercially as a weedicide.
Helps break seed dormancy and strongly promotes seed germination.
Aids in RNA and protein synthesis while delaying aging (senescence) in leaves.
It is the only naturally occurring plant hormone found in a gaseous state.
Also known as the 'stress hormone'; it induces stomatal closure to reduce water loss during extreme drought.

sections.title: Plant Movements and Transpiration
sections.description: Crucial physiological phenomena related to directional growth responses to external stimuli and cellular water loss.

key_concepts.explanation: The directional growth of a plant in response to light. Plant stems exhibit positive phototropism, while roots exhibit negative phototropism.
The directional growth of a plant in response to gravity. Roots exhibit positive geotropism (growing downwards).
The biological process of water loss in the form of vapor from the aerial parts of the plant, primarily through tiny pores called stomata.

important_facts.fact: A potometer is the scientific instrument used to measure the rate of transpiration in plants.
A crescograph is an instrument used to measure plant growth, invented by the renowned Indian scientist Sir J.C. Bose.
